Look: contact sheets of large high-bit-depth footage (#108)

Media frames are shrunk to the cell before the contact sheet is built, so large 10-bit footage no longer overflows; transparent clips keep their alpha. Fixes #103.

commit.message:
Desktop: agents start on Windows again, and an update installs on quit even when reopened at once (#109)

## Agents start on Windows again

**Root cause.** On Windows the desktop app reads the environment from
the registry (`reg query`), so a program installed while the app runs is
found without a restart. `reg query` prints REG_EXPAND_SZ values
unexpanded, for example `ComSpec REG_EXPAND_SZ
%SystemRoot%\system32\cmd.exe`. Until 0.2.1 the registry read failed on
a missing `execFile` import, and the app fell back to the process's own
environment, which Windows had already expanded. 0.2.1 fixed the import,
so agents got the literal `%SystemRoot%\system32\cmd.exe` as `ComSpec`,
and Codex could not start `cmd.exe`.

**Fix.**
- `registryVariables` builds the environment from the registry as a
program started now gets it: the person's variables over the system's,
`%NAME%` expanded, and PATH from `windowsFreshPath` in place of either
`Path`.
- Only REG_EXPAND_SZ values are expanded, as Windows does. A REG_SZ
value that contains `%SystemRoot%` stays literal. `parseRegQuery` can
now list the REG_EXPAND_SZ names, and `registryVariables` and
`windowsFreshPath` expand only those (every value, as before, when no
list is given).

## An update installs on quit even when OpenFilm is opened again right
away

Quitting with an update ready hands it to Squirrel.Mac's ShipIt, which
needs several seconds to swap the app's files and gives up if the app is
running by then. Opened again in those seconds, OpenFilm ran the old
version and the update waited for another quit.

The app now notes the update it has ready (`update-pending.json`), and a
launch on macOS checks it before anything opens:
- while ShipIt is installing it, the launch steps aside and the app
opens again as the new version when ShipIt is done;
- after an install that did not happen, the launch installs it in a
small window that says so, then opens as the new version (not ready
within 45 s, it opens as it is).

That window speaks the language Studio was last shown in. The update
notice and the menu's dialog now say what happens on quit, in all five
languages.

## Testing

- New tests: a REG_SZ value with `%SystemRoot%` stays literal while a
REG_EXPAND_SZ one expands; `ComSpec` is handed on expanded; the
update-launch decisions (`update-launch.test.mjs`).
- `pnpm typecheck`: passes.
- `pnpm --filter @openfilm/desktop test`: 255 passed.
- `pnpm --filter openfilm test`: 1071 passed, 4 skipped.
- `node scripts/audit-public.mjs --no-secrets`: no findings.
- Changesets: both patch.

commit.message:
Desktop: agents from the makers' desktop apps, and never an editor in their place (#110)

## Why

A Windows user pressed Connect for Cursor and the Cursor **editor**
started instead of Cursor's agent: it opened two files named `acp` and
`status` (our `--force acp` and status arguments) and exited. The
editor's launcher (`cursor.cmd` in `resources\app\bin`, found or picked
with Locate) is an npm-style shim, and our shim reading resolved it to
the editor's `resources\app\out\cli.js`, which we ran with our Node.
That script opens the editor with its arguments as files.

## What changed

**Never an editor in place of an agent**
(`apps/desktop/src/agent-installation.mjs`, `notTheAgent`). A program is
refused, both in the automatic search and for Locate, when:
- its path or real path is an editor's launcher location:
`resources/app/bin` (also inside `*.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin`),
`\Programs\cursor\`, `Microsoft VS Code` / `Visual Studio Code`;
- it is (or a `.cmd` resolves to) an editor's `app/out/cli.js`;
- on Windows, it is a window `.exe` (the existing PE header check; a
file whose header can't be read, like a Store app alias, is not
refused);
- for Cursor, it is not in Cursor's own folder (`cursor-agent`, or
Homebrew's `Caskroom/cursor-cli`), for both names `cursor-agent` and
`agent`.

The search now walks folders one by one for every agent, so a refused
file doesn't hide the real agent further down the PATH. A launcher
chosen earlier with Locate is ignored. Locate shows why it refused
(`app`, `not-cursor-agent`) in five languages. The diagnostic report
marks such files.

**Cursor on Windows**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-agent` is searched. A
`.cmd` that runs a Node bundled inside its package (not npm's `node.exe`
beside the shim) is started as the shim itself, so Cursor's agent runs
on its own Node. Its native modules are built for that Node.

**Copies inside the makers' apps**:
- Claude Code on Windows:
`%APPDATA%\Claude\claude-code\<version>\[<build>\]claude.exe`, and the
same folder of the Store app
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Claude_*\LocalCache\Roaming\Claude\claude-code`).
The newest version wins.
- OpenCode on macOS: `OpenCode.app/Contents/Resources/opencode-cli` (it
serves `acp`). It is used when no other OpenCode is found, or when it is
newer than the one on the PATH, the same way Codex in its app works. Its
version comes from `opencode-cli.version` beside it, npm's package,
Homebrew's folder, or `--version`. Locate on `OpenCode.app` picks it.

**Installed only the maker's app** (`desktopApp`, `AGENT_INSTALLERS`,
`openAgentInstaller`, roster `install`, Settings → Agents):
- When an agent's CLI is not found, its desktop app is detected cheaply,
without starting anything: macOS bundles in /Applications and
~/Applications (`Cursor.app`, `Kimi*.app`, `CodeBuddy*.app`,
`MiniMax*.app`, VS Code with a `github.copilot*` extension), and Windows
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<name>`. The row then says "The Cursor app is
installed, but connecting needs Cursor's command-line agent."
- An agent with a confirmed official installer shows an Install button.
It opens a confirm step that shows the exact command, then runs it in
Terminal (macOS) or in a PowerShell window (Windows), the same way the
app opens a window for an agent's own sign-in. The agent is looked for
again every few seconds, and on window focus, until it appears. Agents
without an installer still open their install page.

| Agent | macOS / Linux | Windows | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cursor | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash` | `irm
'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' \| iex` |
https://cursor.com/docs/cli/installation |
| GitHub Copilot | `curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install \| bash` |
`winget install GitHub.Copilot` |
https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/set-up/install-copilot-cli |
| CodeBuddy | `curl -fsSL https://www.codebuddy.cn/cli/install.sh \|
bash` | `irm https://www.codebuddy.cn/cli/install.ps1 \| iex` |
https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/cli/installation |
| Qwen Code | `curl -fsSL
https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh
\| bash` | `irm
https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1
\| iex` | https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code |
| Kimi | `curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh \| bash`
| `irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 \| iex` |
https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code-cli/guides/getting-started.html
|
| MiniMax Code | `curl -fsSL
https://filecdn.minimax.chat/public/install.sh \| bash` | `irm
https://filecdn.minimax.chat/public/install.ps1 \| iex` |
https://agent.minimax.io/docs/cli/quick-start |

The native scripts are used instead of npm, so a person with no Node can
install. The installers' own folders are searched on Windows:
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\codebuddy\bin` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qwen-code\bin`,
because neither installer reliably puts its folder on the user PATH.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm --filter @openfilm/desktop test` (259 pass);
`pnpm --filter openfilm test` (1074 pass, 4 skipped); `node
scripts/audit-public.mjs --no-secrets` (no findings).
- New fixture tests cover each refusal rule: the editor `.cmd` →
`out/cli.js`, a launcher in an app's `resources/app/bin` linked from a
bin folder, VS Code's folder, a window `.exe`, a stray `cursor-agent`,
Homebrew's cursor-cli, a launcher chosen earlier, and Locate refusing
without starting the program. They also cover the Windows Cursor shim,
Claude's Windows and Store paths, OpenCode.app, desktop app detection,
the installer commands, and the roster's install wait.
- On this Mac, `OpenCode.app/Contents/Resources/opencode-cli` was
checked by hand: `--version` gives `opencode v2.0.24`, `acp --help`
works, and `opencode-cli.version` holds `2.0.24`.

## Unverified on Windows

- The Claude app's Claude Code folders on Windows (`%APPDATA%` and the
Store app's `Packages\Claude_*`), and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AnthropicClaude`
as the sign that the Claude app is installed.
- The contents of Cursor's
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-agent\{agent,cursor-agent}.cmd`. It is started
through cmd.exe either way, unless it names a script without its own
Node.
- The desktop app folder names under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` for Kimi,
CodeBuddy and MiniMax.
- The PowerShell installer flow end to end. The sign-in path it reuses
is the existing one.
